original_question: For the sphere S^n, let S^+_2 be the family of non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries, that is, 180-degree rotations about lines through the center. Is ms_r(S^n, S^+_2) = 1/r^2 for all n, r > 1? Equivalently, does every measurable r-coloring of S^n contain a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line through the center of the sphere?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Question 5.6: the open problem asking whether the 1/r^2 lower bound considered just before the question for regular polyhedra and the symmetry family S_2^+ also holds for spheres S^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient object S^n, the intended symmetry family as non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries (half-turns about lines through the center), and the measurable-coloring reformulation in terms of monochromatic subsets symmetric with respect to such a line. It also targets the threshold 1/r^2 that Question 5.6 is about. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
missing_details: The paper’s official target is best read as the lower-bound question ms_r(S^n, S_2^+) ≥ 1/r^2, not the stronger equality statement; this follows from the preceding phrase about 'the same inequality', the 'More precisely' reformulation, and the definition of ms_r in Section 3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
S^n is not just an abstract sphere: in the paper it is endowed with the unique probability Borel measure invariant under the orthogonal group O(n+1). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
A measurable r-coloring means that every color class is measurable for that Borel measure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
The symmetric subset sought should itself be measurable, because ms_r is defined via measurable symmetric subsets. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

The notation immediately before Question 5.6 uses S_2^+ for the family of non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries; your draft’s S^+_2 is mathematically clear but not the paper’s order of indices. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

The geometric phrase 'with respect to some line through the center' means invariance under the 180° rotation about that line, i.e. an involutive orientation-preserving isometry, not reflection in a line. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
refined_question: Let S^n ⊂ R^(n+1) be the unit n-sphere, equipped with its O(n+1)-invariant probability Borel measure, and let S_2^+ be the family of all non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries of S^n, equivalently the rotations by π about lines through the origin. For integers n,r > 1, is ms_r(S^n, S_2^+) ≥ 1/r^2?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every measurable r-coloring of S^n, must there exist a monochromatic measurable subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is invariant under some 180° rotation about a line through the center of the sphere?
justification: Sections 2 and 3 supply the needed definitions: symmetry measure space, measurable symmetric subset, measurable r-coloring, and the maximal symmetry number ms_r(X,S). Section 4 fixes the sphere S^n with its invariant probability Borel measure. Immediately before Question 5.6 in Section 5, the paper introduces the family S_2^+ as the non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries, and Question 5.6 then asks whether the corresponding 1/r^2 lower bound holds on spheres. The main paper-faithful correction to your draft is replacing equality by the lower-bound question, while making the measure and measurability assumptions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
